tweets.text:
I’m being pitched a new inference neocloud company on average every two days. No exaggeration. I take every entrepreneur seriously and I look deeply into each.

But it’s hard to fathom this being sustainable. At the same time, AI Gateway token demand on Vercel has been ~40% MoM compounded since the beginning of the year. No signs of stopping.

One way to reconcile this is that compute is the new economy, and tokens the new energy unit. There’s a new Industrial Revolution taking place. Every aspect of our lives is being replatformed on top of this new system that enhances everything. More like an “oil rush” than a “gold rush”: it’s durable, not a fad.

In the short term, I anticipate more expansion, followed by consolidation due to economies of scale, cybersecurity and enterprise requirements (ZDR and cyber being a hot topic for inference providers), capital requirements, and an evolving regulatory landscape.

tweets.text:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.
tweets.summary_zh: 我们正进入一个新的 AI时代，这些智能助手不仅能快速回答问题，还能在复杂任务中协作。未来，我们可以给它们设定目标，它们会自动设计出最佳解决方案并不断改进，特别是在工程等领域率先应用。这将极大地提升工作效率，让AI完成以前人类无法做到的事情。

tweets.text:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.
tweets.summary_zh: 我们正进入一个新的人工智能助手时代，这些助手不仅能快速回答问题，还能在复杂任务中合作工作。它们将能根据设定的目标自主设计解决方案，并不断改进。比如，你可以让它们改善客户入驻流程，降低业务风险，或者持续提升安全性。这样的智能系统能完成以前人类无法实现的工作，未来的工作效率将大大提升。

tweets.text:
My top 5 takeaways from @nateparrott on how to get Claude to design without AI slop:

1. Give Claude context upfront.

Share screenshots, pages you like, and your past work. For an existing product, have Claude rebuild the real screens from code.

2. Research familiar UX patterns.

For hard layout problems, ask Claude to research familiar products that solve something similar and note the layouts people already know how to use.

3. Make Claude aware of its design biases.

"The model has no idea what its own biases are." In your design.md or another file, consider discouraging Claude's tells like serif text, off-white backgrounds, and card-edge bars.

4. Start with wireframes.

Have Claude create wireframes first and give it feedback to nail your core user flows before going deep on fonts and colors.

5. Ask for multiple options, then remix them.

Ask Claude for 5 options for key screens with different fonts, colors, and styles. Then pick the parts you like and ask it to remix and create 5 more options.

📌 Watch the full episode now: https://t.co/HPX5HjXafX

Also available as a written post: https://t.co/jcofmkQc01
tweets.summary_zh:
从 @nateparrott 那里学到的如何让 Claude（一个 AI 设计助手）设计得更好的五个要点：

1. 提前给 Claude 足够的背景信息，比如喜欢的页面、截图和自己过去的作品。
2. 让 Claude 研究一些大家熟悉的用户体验（UX）设计模式，特别是在复杂布局上。
3. 让 Claude 知道它自己的设计偏见，比如避免使用衬线字体（有装饰的字体）和特定的背景颜色。
4. 先让 Claude 画出线框图（基础设计图），并针对用户体验给予反馈，确认重要的使用流程。
5. 要求 Claude 提供多个设计选项，然后挑选喜欢的部分再让它进行改进。

tweets.text:
The chart of token spend per employee still has no ceiling in sight. And the closer you are to AI right now the deeper the sense is that we’re actually still in the early part of the curve of token use and adoption. 

This summer and fall’s model releases have continued to push the state of the art forward at a rate that already felt hard to maintain. As a result, for most productive use-cases the models are only now starting to actually work, and the feeling is that things will only accelerate from here.

Coding, in retrospect, was basically trash even 12 months ago. Now it’s finally starting to get good. And now that coding is actually working, you’re getting tool and computer use, which open up a wide variety of knowledge work domains that weren’t possible to throw agents at before.

Once you have agents that can code, use computers, leverage any tool out there, and understand a variety of domains, you can begin to throw them at a wide variety of knowledge work tasks that were hard to bring automation to across finance, life sciences, cyber, and more. So that brings agents to a broad set of work that we’re not really using them in yet at scale. 

Then comes the new form factors of agents. Agent swarms and background agents are going to eat up vastly more tokens than anything we can imagine. You’ll have agents running in most enterprises workflows processing data, validating work, doing research, providing decision support, and so on. And we’ll have swarms that fan out in parallel in areas like cyber, life sciences, coding, and more.

So basically tokens are only going up from here.

tweets.text:
Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf.

A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms (and 0.4 ms for @jack's "setting up my twttr" 😁).

X is the global town square, and the medium is the message. Being able to preview what things will look like before posting is great for both humans and agents.

Rendering with xeet is is 100x-1000x faster than booting up a browser and taking a screenshot, yet it's just as accurate.

It reproduces Blink & HarfBuzz text shaping, 1/64px line breaking, RTL bidi, 28 Chirp font subsets, CJK/Math/Emoji fallbacks, "Show more" rules, etc. It's the kind of thing that would be wildly impractical, if not impossible, for a human engineer to pull off.

Except 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝 is structured as an "autorepo." An oracle boots up Chrome, and verifies tens of thousands of text layout rules. A CI canary then watches the evolution of the original, and files signed PRs for agents to act on. It was conceived from the ground up around 'verification engineering', and the result speaks for itself.

Enjoy!

tweets.text:
AI models are inevitably going to keep getting better and better at all coding, tool and computer use, math, and other coding-related tasks. As a result, agents that can use software to do their work, or generate code from scratch, will improve at a faster rate than all other domains of knowledge work.

On one hand that could mean that only a small subset of work can get automated. But probably what happens is that more and more work just becomes coding-shaped to adapt to what agents are good at.

You can see it in the most recent examples of model releases in the past couple of months, where agents can generate code that becomes animated videos, games, 3D models for products, and so on. We also know that tool use gives agents the ability to work with much of the same software that people already work with. This helps in cyber, life sciences, finance, and a number of other domains.

Our mental model traditionally has been that the models have to be able to know everything about anything to generate value, but in reality they *really* have to know how to use or generate software effectively combined with deep domain expertise to make the right judgment calls inside of workflows. 

When you have that powerful combination, almost everything else gets unlocked. This is why the acceleration of agents in knowledge work is only going to increase from here.

传统观念认为，AI 需要了解所有知识才能产生价值，但实际上，它们更需要有效地使用软件以及深厚的领域专业知识，这样才能在工作流程中做出正确的判断。一旦具备这种强大的组合，其它领域也会随之受益。因此，AI 在知识工作中的加速发展只会越来越快。

tweets.text:
What happens to frameworks in the agents era? to component libraries? to @shadcn? 

The answer is: we need to drill deeper. Delete the part, optimize, accelerate, automate.

UI SDK is like the x86 instruction set for agents to build new UI components spontaneously. 

Agents are the new design engineers, and they're ready to build *anything* you ask, tailored to your usecase. High-level, rigid, single-framework abstractions are like kryptonite for what is essentially an infinite, untiring creation machine.

I think we've found someone that allows us to have the cake and eat it too. A decades-long dream. UI SDK is packaged behaviors that give us accessibility, performance, cohesion, saving us tokens, errors and effort, but with absolutely zero limitations and tradeoffs for what UIs we can generate.

Enjoy!

tweets.text:
I look at what I do with Fable 5.2 in the cracks of my week and think: this would've taken five people and $200,000.

Then I look at what my team does with the same AI.

Last week, between meetings, I analyzed our customer survey, made a game for our team, spotted an opportunity to sell @Every to teams, built a CRM, and started reaching out.

Look at that and you might ask: Why would I need a team at all?

The chart seems to agree. On OpenAI's GDPval benchmark, AI went from beating human experts 12.4% of the time in 2024 to around 83% in 2026. That's the aggregate view of the future of work: gather a lot of data and extrapolate a trend line.

But the aggregate misses something. To see it, you have to get intimate: zoom in on one real situation, with all its messiness, and extrapolate from there.

We gave everyone at Every access to the same customer survey and the same AI models.

• I found an opportunity to sell to teams.
• @poojary_yash saw that first-time subscribers were churning because we send too much email.
• @dabrundage noticed that many of our readers feel lonely: they're excited about AI, but people around them think they're crazy.
• @jackcheng turned the results into a Claymation game show.

Could you ask Claude to produce what each of them found? Maybe. But generating possibilities is cheap. Knowing which ones matter is hard.

@hammer_mt ran an experiment to predict what I'd say in Slack. When Claude got 400 attempts, it produced an answer like mine 93% of the time. But when it had to rank its own answers, mine landed in its top 10% only around 60% of the time.

Each person on a team is responsible for a different part of the world. That responsibility narrows where they look, and their perspective helps them decide what matters enough to act on. A team explores more possibilities than a single default prompt, and it can take responsibility for what it finds.

The obvious objection: models will get better at ranking. I think they will. But people aren't frozen while that happens. Comparing 2026 Yash with 2027 Claude misses that there will also be a 2027 Yash, with another year of experience, using 2027 Claude.

As models improve and spread, they raise the floor for everyone. The default answer becomes the baseline. The value is in using your perspective and responsibility to push past it.

That's why I think we need to change how we measure AI. Instead of only asking how well a model performs on problems everyone agrees are worth solving, ask: How good is it at doing my work, from my perspective?

The aggregate can show us the capability curve. The intimate helps us see what we might build, and who we might become, as we ride it.

I presented this at Thesis: 2027. The full talk is on the Every podcast:

tweets.text:
There are basically two kinds of companies to build right now.

1. Diffusion of AI
This is the "vertical SaaS" of today. There are a bunch of different models for it (FDE company, rollup, horizontal product) but ultimately it all boils down to the same thing: get AI diffused very close to where the work is being done.

Profound, Cognition, Harvey etc. A lot of great companies will get built here.

2. Frontier of AI
This is where the really interesting action is. Use AI to accelerate scientific progress, then build products from that progress.

It is a harder category to see. But we are seeing a lot more of it at @spc:

- Externa is adding hundreds of new chemical building blocks to proteins, so you can engineer a drug to match the disease instead of settling for what nature gave you.

- Epana Bio is using genomics and AI to design autoimmune therapies that go after the cellular origin of the disease.

- VenomicsAI is doing AI-accelerated drug discovery from venoms.

- Equivariant is doing multi-physics modeling for the semiconductor industry.

(There are always picks-and-shovels for AI as well. Lots of amazing companies in that category.)

Category 2 is not well understood or much talked about externally. It should be because I think that is where the vast majority of model driven returns will come from.

2. **AI前沿**：这是更有趣的领域。利用AI推动科学进步，再从这些进步中开发产品。比如，Externa公司在为蛋白质增加新化学成分，Epana Bio使用基因组学和AI设计治疗自体免疫病的疗法，还有VenomicsAI进行毒液加速药物发现。这一类的公司虽然不常被讨论，但我认为未来将是回报最多的方向。

对于Yves来说，这个项目对Logic Labs（AI公司）非常有帮助，可以加速AI应用的开发和实验。同时，它也为TexTale的品牌营销和产品推荐等方面提供了创新的AI工具，提升了客户的购物体验。作为创意设计从业者，Yves可以利用这个工具探索新的设计理念和创意表达方式。

github_trending.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目主要是为Cursor提供插件规范和官方插件，使开发者能够创建和共享插件，从而扩展Cursor的功能。对Yves来说，这个项目可以帮助Logic Labs在AI领域更好地整合和开发工具，同时也能为TexTale提供更多的创意设计和电商运营支持，例如通过定制插件提升用户体验和品牌互动。

github_trending.description: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and 550+ data providers through one API.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了一种知识基础设施，通过一个API让用户能够搜索、抓取和访问超过550个数据提供者的数据，从而提升智能代理的能力。针对Yves，Logic Labs可能会从中受益，因为它可以帮助开发更智能的AI应用，改善数据获取和分析能力；同时，对于TexTale，利用这些数据可以更好地了解市场趋势和消费者行为，从而优化电商运营和品牌营销策略。

github_trending.description: The official NGINX Open Source repository.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是NGINX的开源代码库，主要用于提供高性能的Web服务器和反向代理服务，可以帮助网站处理大量的访问请求。对于Yves来说，NGINX可以为TexTale的电商平台提供稳定快速的访问体验，提升用户的购物体验，同时也能为Logic Labs在处理AI模型部署时提供支持，确保数据传输的高效和安全。此外，作为创意设计从业者，了解这样高效的技术工具可以帮助他更好地进行项目的规划和实施。

github_trending.description: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference
github_trending.summary_zh: OpenVINO™ 是一个开源工具包，旨在优化和部署人工智能推理，这意味着它可以帮助加速 AI 模型在不同设备上的应用，使其更高效地工作。对 Yves 来说，这个项目可以为 Logic Labs 提供更强大的 AI 技术支持，提升 AI 模型的性能和部署效率，同时也能为 TexTale 的产品创新提供技术基础，助力更智能的电商体验。作为创意设计从业者，Yves 还可以利用 OpenVINO 优化AI应用，使其在设计和用户体验上更加出色。

github_trending.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, Qoder, and Pi. 45 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了一套用于创建图表的设计工具，支持多种类型的图表，使用简单的 HTML 和 SVG 格式，可以方便地用于高质量的视觉呈现。对于Yves来说，这个工具非常适合Logic Labs，在AI行业中进行创意思维的可视化表达，同时也能够帮助TexTale在产品展示和营销中使用精美图表提升吸引力，增强品牌形象。作为一名创意设计从业者，这个项目能够丰富他的设计工具箱，提高工作效率和创作灵感。

github_trending.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个人工智能助手，可以帮助用户在多个平台（如Reddit、X、YouTube等）上研究任何话题，并为其提供一个经过综合整理的总结。对于Yves而言，这个项目对Logic Labs（AI公司）非常有帮助，因为它可以增强其AI工具的研究与分析能力，进而提升创意设计的深度和广度。

github_trending.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个设计用来与Stitch MCP服务器协同工作的智能助手技能库，每个技能都遵循开放标准，能与多种编码助手兼容。对Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI 公司）更有帮助，因为它可以增强AI应用的功能，提升团队在创意设计和开发方面的效率。同时，借助这些智能技能，Yves也可以在TexTale的电商运营中讨论AI技术的应用，打造更智能的顾客体验。
